items.title: Eddie Locke interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York, NY, January 13, 2001
items.q: Zutty Singleton was the other drummer.

ctx.x: So consequently they developed this excellent technique?

They knew they had to — yes. It made you. You were forced to. And that’s one of the things that I really miss when I listen to a lot of drummers. They’ve all got a great technique with the hands, but that part is — I don’t hear that like I used to hear it. No man, those guys had such wonderful touch, and ideas. My first good job was in the Metropole. That was my first big time job, on Seventh Avenue. And they had music from the morning — from noon, they had music from like 3:00 in the afternoon until 4:00 in ©…

the morning. Two bands change. Like we played from three to seven. New band comes out. Bigger bands. You know two. And I’ll never forget when I first started playing there, I thought I was pretty good. Of course, young, flying, right? Zutty Singleton was the other drummer. “Face” he calls everybody.
